evidence: Ran qc/runs/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r3/per-row-review/evidence/14/seedcheck.py over both shipped seed copies (environment/assets/seed_data.json and solution/app/src/seed_data.json, byte-identical sha256 a1c65c806b54da99a37ab2b5f455ede0a9385a09569903fb3a7f3446f7e83740); output in evidence/14/seedcheck_output.txt, ISSUES []. Measured: (1) JSON parses; ids unique across users (10), jobs (3), applications (16); no duplicate user emails. (2) Referential integrity: every job recruiter_id resolves to a recruiter and manager_id to a hiring_manager; every application job_id, message application_id/sender_id, note application_id/author_id, read user_id/application_id resolves; no orphans. (3) Rule consistency vs hireops_rules.md: stages and candidate_status_labels match the section-7 table exactly; interview_limit integers in 1..50; positions contiguous 1..n per (job, stage); Interview occupancy JOB-PLAT 2/3, JOB-DATA 1/2, JOB-DSGN 1/3 (none overfilled); the only REJECTED card APP-301 has rejected_from SCREEN (not HIRED) and a non-blank reason, and no non-rejected card carries reject fields; no duplicate (job, email) pair (Noor on two different jobs is allowed by rules 2); every candidate-account email on an application matches the account name. (4) Conversation authorship obeys section 6: every sender is a recruiter, that job's manager, or the application's own candidate; no observer messages; no blank bodies; timestamps strictly increasing per conversation (APP-101 120 msgs 2026-07-01..07-16). Notes authored by a recruiter or that job's manager (MGR1 on JOB-PLAT, MGR3 on JOB-DSGN, REC1). (5) Read markers: each within 0..message count, each by a participant (no observer marker). Derived unread for Lena on APP-301 = 1, matching functional/prompt.md:25 ('the starting read markers give her 1'); app_context.md:30 '120 messages at the start' matches. (6) Clean: all emails use RFC 2606 reserved .example domains (hireops.example, candidates.example, mail.example); names are generic synthetic; no DOB/phone/address/ID numbers. Pattern scan for <script, HTML tags, javascript:, on*=, 'ignore previous', DROP TABLE, '--', template markers, NUL and password/secret/token/api_key/Hireops!2026: zero hits, so no credential sits in the seed data itself (the demo password appears only in instruction.md, hireops_rules.md:11, app_context.md and the solution's db.js:63 comment-labelled public demo credential, which the skill profile and internal annotation treat as expected brief content, not seed data). generated_note is a benign pointer to /instructions/hireops_rules.md. Note-level observation (not a defect): USR-CAN1's marker on APP-101 is 119 while message #120 is her own, and USR-REC3's marker on APP-301 is 2 while message #3 is her own; a live app would have advanced these on send, but rules 6 'A person's own messages are never unread' makes both yield 0 unread and neither changes any seen mark (REC1=120 covers #120; REC3=2 covers CAN3's #2), so no grader-observable inconsistency results. Attempted counterexamples: a weak app could not exploit the seed (it holds no answer, probe values or credentials); a conforming app that correctly applies 'own messages never unread' reads the same values the protocols cite, and an app counting own messages as unread would already break the public rule, so the seed creates no trap for a conforming alternative. No runtime measurement is required for this static row; the deterministic parse/fixture half belongs to check-fixtures.py in the deterministic review.
